source: design 0013 (5.4a: The secrets file, The failure contract, Forgetting an item, The bounds): every case and outcome is the design's, written by hand in vectors/generator/secrets.js; no reference implementation exists. The generator lays each file out and seals each entry with Node's AES-256-GCM under fixed keys and nonces, which are public test values.

formats.text: A secrets file's bytes: `text` (UTF-8), `text_hex` (any bytes) or `text_repeat` ([unit, count]: the unit repeated). A file the core writes is JSON.stringify(file, null, 2), with no newline after it.
formats.file: { version: 1, keys: { <policy>: { backend, item: <32 hex> | null, sealed: <base64> | null, pending: { backend, item } | null } }, forget: [ { backend, policy, item } ], entries: { <name>: { key: <policy>, nonce: <base64, 12 bytes>, ciphertext: <base64: AES-256-GCM ciphertext, then the 16-byte tag>, binding: { <member>: <text> } } } }. keys by policy (unattended, then user_presence), forget in the order its records were added, entries by name, binding members by name.
formats.aad: An entry's associated data: the ASCII bytes of `freedom-secrets/1`, a zero byte, the entry's name, a zero byte, and the binding's canonical JSON (JSON.stringify of its members in order of name: no space; values are printable ASCII, so only `"` and `\` are escaped).
formats.files: Files in form. `items` is every item the file names, in its order: each key's committed item then its pending one, by policy, then the forget list (what a profile delete records, and what fc-profile's reader finds). `entries` gives each entry's wrapping key, nonce, binding, canonical JSON, associated data (hex) and secret, as the generator sealed it; an entry `sealed_as` another name, binding, key or nonce, or with its last byte `flipped`, was sealed so on purpose. `opens` opens an entry by `name` with the caller's `binding` under `key` (hex): `secret` (text), or `error`: no_entry (no such entry), other_binding (the file binds it to something else: nothing is decrypted) or refused (it doesn't open: another name, binding or key, or a changed byte).
formats.malformed: Texts refused, each with the first `reason` the core finds: too_large (over 128 KiB), json (not UTF-8 JSON), version (no `version` 1), form (a member missing, extra, of another type or out of form), items (more than four items named), entries (more than 32 entries), duplicate (an item id twice, or one nonce twice under one key), key_not_in_use (an entry under a key the file doesn't hold committed), key_unused (a committed key with no entry), not_canonical (in form, but not the text the core writes for it).
formats.transitions: One change to the file `before`. `op`: ["begin_create", policy, backend, item] records item as pending before `create` runs; ["commit", sealed, new_key, old_key | null, put | null] makes the pending item sealed names its policy's key (sealed: { backend, policy, item, blob: base64 | null }), re-wrapping the policy's entries in order of name from old_key to new_key, then writes put under it; ["put", policy, key, put] writes put under the policy's committed key; ["remove", name]; ["settle"], at a profile's open; ["forgotten", item], after its forget answered ok or not_found; ["drop_foreign", backend | null], the backend this OS has. put is { name, binding, secret (text) }; keys are hex. `rng` lists the RNG's draws in order, each one fill of a 12-byte nonce (hex); an RNG past its list fails. The result is `after` (exactly that text, every draw used) or `refused`: forget_backlog, named, not_pending, no_key, other_key, no_entry, entries, secret_size, key_needed, entry_refused or randomness, with nothing changed.
